audit_findings.title: The bridge may treat required operating liquidity as surplus cash
audit_findings.magnitude: unquantified; $179.468 million is added to the bridge, equal to $0.81 per share and 31.9% of base equity value
audit_findings.mechanism: Any required operating-cash reserve must be removed from cash added in the equity bridge.
audit_findings.evidence: Management expects to fund the foregoing obligations primarily from operating cash flows and existing cash, with the revolving credit facility providing added flexibility if needed.
audit_findings.explanation: The addition of the entire cash balance is demonstrated, but the amount that is genuinely excess is not. The exposure is material: excluding the full balance would reduce base value from $2.53 to approximately $1.72 per share. The filing also identifies capital spending, working-capital needs and contractual obligations funded partly from existing cash.
audit_findings.action: Establish a June 30, 2026 minimum cash reserve using monthly working-capital requirements, the remaining 2026 capital program, committed expenditures and restricted balances; rerun the bridge with only excess unrestricted cash.

audit_findings.title: The latest-year anchor may understate recurring maintenance capital
audit_findings.magnitude: unquantified; 2026 guidance of $170-$190 million exceeds 2025 capital expenditures of $148.407 million by $21.593-$41.593 million, or 79%-153% of the $27.2 million anchor
audit_findings.mechanism: Higher normalized maintenance capital reduces recurring owner earnings and every forecast and terminal-value cash flow derived from the anchor.
audit_findings.evidence: We expect 2026 capital expenditures to be directed towards capitalized maintenance of our existing equipment and selected growth opportunities as well as the upgrade to our ERP and supply chain systems.
audit_findings.explanation: A maintenance-capital error is not demonstrated because guidance combines maintenance, growth opportunities and ERP spending. Nevertheless, the gross increase is comparable with or greater than the entire anchor, so even a portion proving recurring could materially lower value. First-half 2026 capital expenditures of $70.837 million do not resolve the issue because management cites equipment-delivery timing and retained full-year guidance of $170-$190 million.
audit_findings.action: Obtain the maintenance, replacement, ERP and growth-capital components for 2025 and 2026, including Pintail's full-year requirements, then rerun all scenarios using normalized recurring maintenance capital.

audit_findings.title: Finite Pintail retention charges may be perpetuated in the anchor
audit_findings.magnitude: $20.312 million pre-tax in FY2025; an additional $14.583 million was filed for the first half of 2026
audit_findings.mechanism: If included without an expiry adjustment, finite acquisition-related employment costs depress anchor OE and are projected into continuing and terminal owner earnings.
audit_findings.evidence: An additional amount totaling $ 37.5 million, ("Redistribution Payments”) paid by the Seller out of Closing Cash, is subject to continued employment with RPC for a period of three years from the Closing Date.
audit_findings.explanation: The three-year service condition and recorded charges are demonstrated, but the record does not establish how the $27.2 million OE calculation treated them. The FY2025 charge equals 74.7% of the anchor, and the 2026 filing confirms it continues, making perpetual treatment materially conservative. It should not simply be removed from all forecast years because payments and economic dilution during the remaining service period still require recognition.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile the OE treatment of the Seller Note obligation asset, restricted shares and Redistribution Payments; model the remaining charges through April 2028 and their cessation thereafter, while retaining recurring compensation and dilution.

audit_findings.title: A one-time SERP dissolution tax effect may depress anchor OE
audit_findings.magnitude: approximately $18 million taxable gain and a filed $3.778 million long-term-retirement-plan tax reconciling item; if $3.778 million was perpetuated, computed base value is understated by approximately $53.1 million or $0.24 per share
audit_findings.mechanism: A nonrecurring tax charge left in anchor OE reduces all projected owner earnings and terminal value.
audit_findings.evidence: The liquidation of COLI assets resulted in a taxable gain of approximately $ 18 million that has been included in the income tax provision for the year ended December 31, 2025.
audit_findings.explanation: The SERP dissolution, COLI liquidation and taxable gain are demonstrated. Whether the OE calculation normalized the resulting tax effect is unresolved. The filed $3.778 million tax item is 13.9% of the $27.2 million anchor and would therefore be material if perpetuated.
audit_findings.action: Trace the $3.778 million tax-reconciliation item and related current/deferred tax entries into the OE worksheet; if included, remove only the incremental dissolution-related tax and rerun all scenarios.

audit_findings.title: Finance-lease asset consumption may escape the OE capital charge
audit_findings.magnitude: $0.952 million FY2025 finance-lease amortization and $1.143 million principal paid; using the larger amount gives a computed base sensitivity of approximately $16.1 million or $0.07 per share
audit_findings.mechanism: An omitted finance-lease replacement or principal charge would overstate OE after finance-lease amortization is added back with total D&A.
audit_findings.evidence: The components of finance lease are included in depreciation and amortization and interest expense; operating lease expenses are included in costs of goods sold, and selling, general and administrative expenses in the Consolidated Statements of Operations as disclosed below.
audit_findings.explanation: The OE omission itself is not demonstrated. On the disclosed scale, the larger annual cash measure is only 4.2% of the $27.2 million anchor and would change base value by about 2.8%, from $2.53 to roughly $2.46 per share. That is immaterial beside the $3.97 per-share gap between base value and the $6.50 market price and cannot change the valuation conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Confirm the OE worksheet's treatment of the $0.952 million amortization, $0.887 million of new finance-lease ROU assets and $1.143 million principal payment; correct any omission in the next model refresh.

audit_findings.title: Unestimable tax-audit exposures could be an unrecorded senior claim
audit_findings.mechanism: An unrecorded assessment would reduce cash or create a senior liability in the equity bridge and could reduce OE through taxes, interest or penalties.
audit_findings.evidence: These audits involve issues that could result in unfavorable outcomes that cannot be currently estimated.
audit_findings.explanation: No loss beyond recorded probable and estimable amounts is demonstrated. The June 2026 filing says certain notified matters were resolved without material impact, but it continues to disclose other audit outcomes that cannot be estimated. With no exposure range, the record cannot establish whether the remaining claim could materially affect value.
audit_findings.action: Obtain an audit-by-audit schedule of asserted bases, jurisdictions, periods, correspondence, reserves, potential interest and penalties, and subsequent settlements; rerun the bridge and OE only for exposures supported by that evidence.
